title: The visual gate flakes on three pixels of corner antialiasing
foundBy: session agent, while re-recording the dashboard captures for CUI-024
details:
`visual:compare` reported `dark/card-group.png` at 3 differing pixels on one run and at 0 on the next, with the working tree byte for byte the same. The three sit at (973, 378), (973, 379) and (972, 380), the bottom right corner of the last card, and each is one unit on one or two channels: `16,21,26` against `17,22,27`.

It is rare. Eleven runs of the same container on the same machine produced it once. It did not reproduce in five clean-tree runs, and appeared once in six runs with an unrelated change to the dashboard demo applied.

This matters because the comparison allows no difference at all, which CUI-052 justified on the ground that runs in this image are deterministic to the pixel. That was measured as 104 byte-identical captures across two runs, and eleven runs are enough to see that it is not quite true. A gate that fails once in ten runs for no reason teaches a reader to re-run it, which is the habit that lets a real failure through.

What is not established is the cause. A one-unit shift at a rounded corner is where a rasteriser rounds, and whether that turns on compositing timing or on something in the page is unmeasured. The fallback CUI-052 already names is a small pixel floor rather than a return to the perceptual threshold, and a floor of a handful of pixels would absorb this while still failing on the 20 pixel change that the `wrap: true` fix in CUI-027 produced. Whether to spend that headroom is the open question.

notes.text:
The same failure reproduces on `dark/interaction-split-pane-drag.png`, and far more often than the eleven runs this record started from. It is bistable rather than random. Two renderings alternate, and `npm run visual:compare` returned one or the other with the working tree unchanged.

The eight differing pixels sit at x=972 and x=973, on the top right and the bottom right corner, at one or two units per channel. That is the signature this record already describes for `card-group`, at the same x.

Re-recording is the hazard worth naming. A `visual:capture` run recorded the minority rendering, after which the gate failed two runs in three. Restoring that one file from the previous commit put the majority rendering back, and it failed one run in four. A baseline refresh can land on the wrong side of the pair, and turn a rare flake into a near permanent failure.
